title: Standby Host Evacuation Orchestrator — dynamic eviction buffer to preserve throughput during node maintenance
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Scheduled node maintenance and OS/kernel upgrades currently rely on blunt draining that can temporarily reduce per-tenant throughput and trigger SLO alerts for Dedicated customers. Objective: Implement a coordinator that uses a configurable eviction buffer and standby host orchestration to evacuate a node in stages while preserving committed throughput contracts. The orchestration should reserve temporary soft capacity, route new traffic to standby hosts, pre-warm KV caches where possible, and coordinate with autoscaler + scheduler to avoid over-eviction. This ticket covers design + MVP implementation for the runtime/controller pieces required to run staggered evacuations across failure domains (AZ/rack) with automated rollback triggers.
comments: 2026-01-11 — Kickoff: scoped to dedicated fleets only; private deployments will be follow-up. Agreed to focus MVP on cross-zone-aware evacuations and a configurable eviction buffer (default 5% of fleet capacity).

2026-01-15 — Design review (PM + Infra): PM requested explicit customer-visible hooks (maintenance window start/finish timestamps + SLA impact estimate). Added 'maintenance_window' metadata to plan. Action: add API for querying active evacuations.

2026-01-20 — Simulation results: Monte Carlo sim over 30 days with realistic request arrival traces shows median throughput dip of 0.6% with 5% eviction buffer; 95th percentile dip 2.9%. Attached perf notes in Drive link. Decision: expose buffer as percent and absolute token-per-second reservation.

2026-01-26 — Engineering sync: Marco implemented proof-of-concept controller that: computes candidate evacuation plan, acquires standby leases, signals scheduler; next: integrate with autoscaler to temporarily scale up standby pool when needed.
2026-01-30 — PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pulls/1286 — basic controller + unit tests. Need e2e harness to validate KV pre-warm semantics and per-tenant throughput shaping.

2026-02-03 — Design feedback from Reliability: add automatic rollback if per-tenant p50 latency increases >20% for >2 minutes OR if throughput loss >5% sustained for 5 minutes. Added to acceptance criteria.
2026-02-05 — Blocker noted: autoscaler race when multiple evacuations overlap in small fleets. Mitigation: introduce global evacuation queue and tokenized standby capacity. Follow-up subtask created.
acceptance_criteria: Controller can schedule and execute a staggered evacuation plan for a node while ensuring the configured eviction buffer (percent or TPS) is respected
End-to-end test: during a maintenance window with a simulated load pattern, total fleet throughput loss is <=3% (median) and <=6% (95th) compared to baseline for fleets >= 50 nodes
Per-tenant throughput contracts (reserved TPS) are maintained — no single tenant experiences >10% allocation reduction during evacuation
Automatic rollback triggers: p50 latency increase >20% for 2+ minutes OR sustained throughput drop >5% for 5+ minutes causes controller to abort and revert evacuation
Exposes API endpoints for: listing active evacuations, querying planned capacity reservations, and cancelling an evacuation
Integration with autoscaler to temporarily request standby capacity and release it after maintenance completes
End-to-end e2e test in staging that includes KV cache pre-warm step and validates request routing to standby hosts
Operational metrics emitted: evacuation_start/finish, planned_buffer_pct, standby_capacity_acquired, rollback_triggered_reason
notes: MVP scope excludes private on-prem autopilot; those require separate KV warming hooks and network considerations
We should coordinate with PS teams for early adopters — suggested pilot: two existing Dedicated customers on us-east-1 with fleets >= 60 nodes
Follow-up work: fair-share throttler to avoid tenant head-of-line blocking during simultaneous evacuations
